title: Cost Economizer: staged ingress with operator-led canary and rollback playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Deliver a staged activation framework for 'Economizer' recommendations (batching + KV cache suggestions) that safely applies config changes via a controlled ingress: tiny canaries, operator-led approvals at safety fences, and a documented rollback playbook. This ticket spans controller logic, console UX for approvals, telemetry gates, and an operator runbook for escalations. The goal is to enable low-friction cost reductions while keeping latency and error budgets protected.
acceptance_criteria:
- Controller can apply a recommendation to a 1% canary cohort and escalate to staged percentage ramps (1%, 5%, 20%, 100%)
- Metric gates: p99 latency delta <= 5ms vs baseline, error rate delta <= +0.2%, cost/unit reduction >= 6% during each ramp step
- Approval UI allows operator to approve/hold/rollback with an audit trail and link to telemetry snapshot
- Automatic rollback triggers implemented and exercised via integration test that simulates p99 spike
- Documentation and runbook merged with Playbook and Console release notes
proposed_solution_summary: Implement a 'Staged Ingress Controller' that can programmatically create cohorts and attach recommended config patches; integrate with Console to surface candidate diffs, show simulated impact (from offline evaluator), and provide one-click operator controls. Add telemetry gates in the routing layer and enforce circuit-breaker-style halting logic. Provide a pre-baked rollback playbook and a canary observability dashboard template for SRE/PEM use.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (lab): simulate workload with offline evaluator; Phase 1 (pilot): internal teams (dev+staging) on 0.5% traffic for 48h; Phase 2 (mini-canary): 1% production traffic for 24h with SRE on-call watching; Phase 3: 5% for 48h with automated checks; Phase 4: 20% then 100% if all gates pass. Each phase requires operator ACK via Console except Phase 0.
canary_policy:
- Start size: 1% of requests weighted by customer shard
- Metrics window: 10-minute rolling windows, 3 consecutive windows to pass a step
- Pass conditions: (p99_latency_delta_ms <= 5) AND (error_rate_delta_percent <= 0.2) AND (cost_reduction_percent >= 6)
- Fail conditions: breach of any pass condition for two windows OR manual abort by operator
- Safety fence: automatic pause on infra anomalies (OOM, GPU allocation failures)
approval_workflow:
- Suggestion generated by Optimize engine -> shows in Console 'Economizer candidates' panel with impact simulation and risk score
- Operator flow: review diff, run simulated dry-run, then click 'Start Canary' (requires SRE or on-call approval)
- At step transitions, operator receives a Slack notification with 'Approve / Hold / Rollback' buttons. Approvals are recorded with user, timestamp, and rationale.
- High-risk suggestions (risk score > 0.7 or customer_impact=high) require dual approval: SRE + Product.
rollback_playbook:
- Automatic rollback triggers: threshold breach in telemetry gates -> controller initiates rollback to previous config; sends alert + creates incident ticket with prefilled diagnostics
- Manual rollback steps for operator: Console -> Economizer candidate -> 'Force Rollback' -> select target snapshot (controller maintains last-3 snapshots) -> confirm.
- Post-rollback checks: validate p95/p99 back to baseline within 30 minutes, run 'health-check suite' (end-to-end smoke tests), and open a postmortem if rollback occurred in production.
telemetry_and_alerts:
- Dashboard: economizer/canary/<id> shows p50/p95/p99, error rates, token cost per request, successful/failed requests, KV cache hit rate
- Alerts: Canary-Fail (when gate fails), Latency-Regress (p99 delta > 10ms), Cost-Neutrality-Failure (cost reduction < 2% after 72h)
- Tracing: sample traces pinned to canary cohort for deep dive
- Logs: audit trail of approvals and config diffs stored in central audit log
